prompt:
Design and implement the migration architecture for the Chicago management estate described in `fixtures/estate-inventory.json`. The destination is VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0.1.0: VMware Aria Operations, VMware Aria Automation, and VMware Aria Operations for Logs must become VCF Operations, VCF Automation, and VCF Operations for Logs while preserving every supported content and configuration item. This is an architecture deliverable, not an explanatory report.

Before implementing it, research current Broadcom-published material covering all four of these subjects: supported product migration and upgrade paths, content and configuration compatibility, end-of-general-support boundaries, and the vSAN OSA/ESA host-and-network tradeoff. Record each Broadcom source consulted as an object in `research-sources.json` using `title`, `publisher`, `url` (HTTPS), `accessedOn` (YYYY-MM-DD), and `supports`. Use only these `supports` subject labels: `migration-path`, `content-compatibility`, `support-boundary`, and `storage-network`.

Build `VcfMigrationArchitecture/VcfMigrationArchitecture.psd1` and `.psm1` as a PowerShell 7 module. Export `New-VcfMigrationInstallerSpec`, which accepts `-InventoryPath` and `-OutputPath`, consumes the estate inventory, and deterministically writes `installer-spec.json`. Declare `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.Installer` as a module dependency in the manifest and use its VCF Installer operation discovery to include the `POST /v1/sddcs/validations`, `POST /v1/sddcs/resources-calculation`, and `POST /v1/sddcs` bindings. Do not vendor any VMware module or assembly.

The generated `installer-spec.json` must validate against `spec/vcf-migration-installer-spec.schema.json`. It must compare both OSA and ESA using supported host counts and physical network requirements, select the design that meets the stated requirements, name its required network changes, and place and size every target management component. Its ordered migration plan must name every inventoried source product and exact version, its supported target component and version and migration mode, account exactly once for every inventoried content item as carried forward or abandoned, and attach one or more concrete technical gates to every step. Include the researched support boundary for every source product and make dependencies point only to earlier steps. Keep all paths relative to this repository and put no credentials in the outputs.

Run the module to create the checked-in `installer-spec.json`. The acceptance command is `pwsh -NoLogo -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File tests/verify.ps1`. Do not modify anything under `fixtures/`, `spec/`, or `tests/`, and do not submit a narrative migration document.
